findings.title: Test does not assert send() throws closed_error on refusal
findings.claim: The try/catch around the hook passes whether send() succeeds or throws closed_error; the only assertion is !st.put_after_close, so a regression where send() silently drops the frame would still pass.

findings.title: Failed assertion or exception during test skips close-parking cleanup
findings.claim: If the BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL at :2000 fails, the hook throws something other than closed_error, or sink_closed.get() fails, the cleanup (release_close.set_value(), sink_closed.get(), server_done.get()) is skipped, leaving the connection parked until timeout or an abort in ~sink_impl.

findings.title: close_entered_cv.wait() has no timeout
findings.claim: If a regression stalls before data_sink::close() is reached, the test hangs until test.py's 300s timeout instead of failing cleanly.

findings.title: Drain and server-side stream closing paths are untested
findings.claim: The test fires the hook only after queue_drained is already ready, so the case the drain exists for (a frame queued just before the flag) is never covered; server_factory's hooks are installed but never fired, so server-side stream connections and close_source()-triggered stream_close() have no test.

findings.title: Doc says dropping an unclosed sink 'is an error', understating it aborts the process
findings.claim: It is actually a SEASTAR_ASSERT in ~sink_impl, which aborts the process, and the doc should say so.

findings.title: Doc claim that reading until it throws is the only way to close the source is inaccurate
findings.claim: close_source() only runs on eof or when stream_receive fails; an exception from unmarshall in process_one_buffer() does not close the source, and closing the client or aborting the connection are also other ways to release it.

findings.title: Doc overstates that shutdown only happens once both stream halves are closed
findings.claim: Closing the client (abort_all_streams), connection errors, and abort() also shut it down, and the same doc's line 49 already says so.

findings.title: Comment inaccurately implies nothing waits on _outgoing_queue_ready anymore
findings.claim: stop_send_loop() still does when_all on _outgoing_queue_ready and _sink_closed_future; it only works because it gets the ready placeholder from std::exchange, which the comment should state instead of claiming nothing waits on it.

findings.title: ignore_ready_future() silently drops a failed queue entry without logging
findings.claim: The failure was already delivered to that entry's caller or the connection was aborted, so this is acceptable, but a debug log would help diagnosis.

findings.title: PR body does not explain the claimed unflushed frame found on the parent client
findings.claim: The PR body says the same unflushed-frame issue was found on the parent client, but the fix only covers stream connections and the PR does not explain the parent-side frame.

findings.title: Test hard-codes buffer size 8192 instead of forwarding buffer_size()
findings.claim: The test could forward buffer_size() instead of hard-coding the value 8192.

findings.title: set_reuseaddr/get_reuseaddr are a no-op and hard-coded false instead of forwarded
findings.claim: These methods should forward to the inner socket rather than being a no-op and a hard-coded false.

findings.title: Old one-line comments are now redundant with the new Doxygen blocks
findings.claim: The old '// send data Out...' and '// receive data In...' lines should be folded into the new /// blocks; Doxygen ignores the // lines so docs still attach correctly, but the old lines are redundant.

findings.title: PR body ends with a Claude-generated attribution line
findings.claim: The PR body ends with '🤖 Generated with Claude Code', which the user's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md forbids in PR descriptions.

findings.title: Commits carry Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers
findings.claim: All three commits (f545c28a, 5e25ebdb, 69da8f5b) carry Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers, violating the same attribution rule; older commits on the base branch having such trailers does not waive it.

findings.title: Fixes #3663 and Refs #3653 issue references do not resolve
findings.claim: These references appear in the PR body and in f545c28a's commit message, but gh issue view returns 'Could not resolve' for both; they should be qualified with the owner/repo or Fixes will not close the intended issue.

findings.title: Fix and its regression test are split across separate commits
findings.claim: The fix (f545c28a) and its test (5e25ebdb) are in separate commits; bisect is unaffected but cherry-picking only the fix drops the regression test, and squashing them would be cleaner.

findings.title: Validation claims in PR body are not backed by any CI link or log
findings.claim: The PR body's claims that the test passes and fails without the fix are not backed by any CI link or log.

findings.title: Generic test_ names hide that these classes exist to park close()
findings.claim: test_data_sink_impl, test_sink_state, and the two socket classes exist only to park close() and record late put() calls, but their generic test_ names don't say this; something like close_parking_* would.

findings.title: test_connected_socket_impl hand-forwards ~16 methods, will drift if interface changes
findings.claim: No existing helper can park close(), so a forwarding base class or a 'park close' hook on the loopback error injector would remove this hand-forwarded duplication.

findings.title: const_cast used in a const negotiate() instead of a mutable member
findings.claim: The file's own precedent is using mutable (cfactory::use_compression); hooks should be declared mutable and the const_cast dropped.

findings.title: Unused server_factory captured hooks lack an explanatory comment
findings.claim: server_factory is needed so the server negotiates the 'HOOK' compressor, but its captured hooks are never used; a comment should explain that.

findings.title: Fragile reference into hooks vector could dangle if it reallocates
findings.claim: size()==2u ties the test to the number of negotiations, and auto&... = hooks.back() would dangle if a later negotiation reallocated the vector; copying the std::function would be safer.

findings.title: Fixed 10-yield polling loop is an arbitrary, non-deterministic bound
findings.claim: Ten yield()s has no guarantee of crossing a reactor poll; a signal set in put() (like close_entered_cv) would make the wait deterministic.

findings.title: Pass-through compressor duplicates an existing one in the same file
findings.claim: It repeats the pass-through already implemented in test_compressor_empty_frames' tracker::factory.

findings.title: New wait in stream_close() has no timeout or cancellation described
findings.claim: stream_close() now waits on _outgoing_queue_ready before closing the buffer with no timeout of its own; this is not described in the PR and not a regression versus the old flushing write_buf.close(), but it is also untested.

findings.title: PR body loosely compares the drain's wait to send(), but they differ
findings.claim: The PR says the drain waits on _outgoing_queue_ready 'the way send() does', but unlike send() it uses then_wrapped and ignores a failed chain; the code comment at rpc.cc:566 describes this correctly.
